Title: Diagnosis of test `testEscapeJavaWithSlash`
Details: 
The test `testEscapeJavaWithSlash` in `StringEscapeUtilsTest` is designed to verify that the method `StringEscapeUtils.escapeJava(String)` does not escape the forward slash character ('/').

The test expects the input string `"String with a slash (/) in it"` to remain unchanged after calling `escapeJava`. However, the test fails indicating that `escapeJava` is escaping the '/' character, which according to the test comment, should not happen as '/' is not a valid character to escape in Java strings.

The method `StringEscapeUtils.escapeJava(String)` calls `escapeJavaStyleString(String, boolean)` with `escapeSingleQuotes` set to `false`. This method uses a `StringWriter` and delegates the actual escaping to `escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean)`.

Inside `escapeJavaStyleString(Writer, String, boolean)`, the code iterates over each character in the input string. It performs character checks and writes either the original character or an escaped version to the output writer.

The relevant part concerning the slash character is around lines 243-245 in the method:

```java
case '/' :
    out.write('\\');
    out.write('/');
    break;
```

This explicitly escapes the '/' character by prefixing it with a backslash. This behavior contradicts the expectation in the test, where '/' should not be escaped and should appear as is in the output string.

Thus, the reason for the test failure is that the `escapeJavaStyleString` method currently escapes '/' characters, even though the test expects them to remain unescaped as per valid Java string escape rules.

To fix the test failure, the escape logic for '/' characters in `escapeJavaStyleString` should be altered or removed so that '/' is no longer escaped by the method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
